findings.text: The generic header provides paused single port helpers named inb_p and inw_p and inl_p for input plus outb_p and outw_p and outl_p for output. Input helpers accept a port number and produce a byte or word or long value respectively, while output helpers accept a value plus a port number and produce no result. Each paused helper behaves exactly like its plain counterpart, so no extra delay or ordering is added in this generic form. A self named marker accompanies each helper to record generic availability.

Block port helpers named insb and insw and insl for input plus outsb and outsw and outsl for output move counted sequences of byte or word or long units between a port and a memory buffer. Each accepts a port number plus a buffer pointer plus an element count. Input helpers fill the buffer from the port, while output helpers move from a read only buffer to the port. Translation adds the port number to a shared base named PCI_IOBASE and then uses the matching width specific memory string operation. A self named marker accompanies each helper.

Paused block port helpers named insb_p and insw_p and insl_p plus outsb_p and outsw_p and outsl_p accept the same port plus buffer plus count arguments as their plain forms and keep the same input versus output direction. Each paused helper behaves exactly like its plain block counterpart with no added semantics in the generic header. A self named marker accompanies each helper.

Memory mapped single accessors named ioread8 and ioread16 and ioread32 and ioread64 for reads plus iowrite8 and iowrite16 and iowrite32 and iowrite64 for writes operate on a volatile device address. Read helpers accept the device address and produce an eight or sixteen or thirty two or sixty four bit value respectively. Write helpers accept a value of matching width plus the device address and produce no result. Each helper is equivalent to the corresponding width specific plain memory accessor in this generic configuration, with a self named marker recording availability.

Big endian single accessors named ioread16be and ioread32be and ioread64be plus iowrite16be and iowrite32be and iowrite64be cover sixteen and thirty two and sixty four bit widths, with no eight bit member in this set. Read helpers load through the matching plain width accessor and then reverse byte order before returning. Write helpers reverse byte order of the supplied value before storing through the matching plain width accessor. A self named marker accompanies each helper.

Repeated memory mapped helpers named ioread8_rep and ioread16_rep and ioread32_rep and ioread64_rep plus iowrite8_rep and iowrite16_rep and iowrite32_rep and iowrite64_rep move counted sequences between a device address and a memory buffer. Read variants accept device address plus destination buffer plus count, while write variants accept device address plus read only source buffer plus count. Each helper is equivalent to the matching width specific memory string operation. A self named marker accompanies each helper.

Conversion helpers named virt_to_phys and phys_to_virt and xlate_dev_mem_ptr plus a cast helper named __io_virt define lossless address translation. The first maps a virtual pointer to an integer physical address using a platform absolute conversion named __pa, the second maps an integer physical address back to a virtual pointer using a conversion named __va, and the device translator maps a physical address to a virtual pointer using the same __va conversion. The cast helper reinterprets an I O token as a plain pointer without changing its value. Each conversion helper carries a self named marker.

Mapping helpers named ioremap and ioremap_uc and ioremap_np plus aliases named ioremap_wc and ioremap_wt translate a physical offset plus length into a device address. Two alternative plain forms are shown, one returning the offset value directly as the device address and another requesting a protected mapping that combines the address plus length with an architecture supplied I O page attribute named _PAGE_IOREMAP through a protection aware constructor named ioremap_prot. The uncached and no populate variants always fail by yielding a null pointer in the shown generic forms. The write combining and write through names are aliases of the plain form in both generic headers. Each active helper carries a self named marker.

A port mapping helper named ioport_map accepts a port number plus length, masks the port with a limit named IO_SPACE_LIMIT, yields a null pointer when the masked value exceeds a bound named MMIO_UPPER_LIMIT, and otherwise yields a base named PCI_IOBASE plus the masked port. Companion helpers named ioport_unmap and iounmap and unxlate_dev_mem_ptr accept their pointer arguments and perform no action in the generic forms. Markers named ARCH_HAS_GENERIC_IOPORT_MAP and ARCH_WANTS_GENERIC_PCI_IOUNMAP record that generic mapping and generic PCI unmapping are present. Each active helper carries a self named marker.

A macro named _IOC_TYPECHECK has two alternative forms for deriving a transfer size from a type. One form yields the size of the given type directly. The other yields the size only when the type size equals the size of its second element and is below a power of two bound derived from a constant named _IOC_SIZEBITS, and otherwise yields a marker named __invalid_size_argument_for_IOC. The validated form therefore rejects arrays and oversized types at compile time.
The generic default interrupt count named NR_IRQS has value sixty four.

Interrupt helpers include a canonicalizer named irq_canonicalize plus per CPU frame accessors named get_irq_regs and set_irq_regs. The canonicalizer returns its input unchanged. Retrieval yields the calling CPU current stored exception frame pointer. Installation replaces that pointer with a supplied value and returns the previous pointer, supporting save and restore around nested handling.
A diagnostic enumeration named die_val defines a member named DIE_UNUSED for the unused case and a member named DIE_OOPS with numeric value one for the fault case.
A handover scratch descriptor named kho_scratch holds two fields of type named phys_addr_t, one named addr giving a location and one named size giving an extent.

A permanent mapping index bound named KM_MAX_IDX has two alternative values in the fragments, one with numeric value thirty three and another with numeric value sixteen, reflecting alternative configurations.

Probe exclusion support has enabled and disabled configurations for helpers named __NOKPROBE_SYMBOL and NOKPROBE_SYMBOL and __kprobes and nokprobe_inline. In the enabled form the constructor records a function address in a dedicated blacklist section under a derived symbol name, the wrapper invokes that constructor, the function attribute requests exemption from tracing plus placement in a dedicated probes text section, and the inline marker requires unconditional inlining. In the disabled form the wrapper expands to nothing, the function attribute is empty, and the inline marker is a plain inline request.

Paravirtual helpers named kvm_check_and_clear_guest_paused and kvm_arch_para_features and kvm_arch_para_hints and kvm_para_available provide constant false or zero results in the generic header. The guest paused check always reports false, the feature and hint queries always report numeric zero, and the availability check always reports false, indicating no paravirtual support here.
A CPU local counter type named local_t wraps a single member named a of type named atomic_long_t, giving a distinct type for local operations while reusing atomic storage.

Local counter operations named LOCAL_INIT plus local_read and local_set and local_inc and local_dec and local_add and local_sub plus test variants local_sub_and_test and local_dec_and_test and local_inc_and_test and local_add_negative plus returning variants local_add_return and local_sub_return and local_inc_return plus atomic primitives local_cmpxchg and local_try_cmpxchg and local_xchg and local_add_unless and local_inc_not_zero all delegate to the matching atomic long operation on the wrapped member. Initialization sets the initial value, reads and writes move values, arithmetic updates the counter, test forms report zero or sign outcomes, returning forms yield the new value, and compare exchange forms provide conditional update semantics.

Non atomic local helpers named __local_inc and __local_dec and __local_add and __local_sub implement read plus modify plus write through the plain local read and set operations without atomicity. Callers must provide exclusion against concurrent updates and interrupts where needed, as these helpers offer no locking themselves while the plain local operations delegate to atomic primitives that need no extra lock.

A sixty four bit local counter type named local64_t has two alternative layouts. One wraps a member named a of type named local_t, reusing the local counter implementation. The other wraps a member named a of type named atomic64_t, using direct atomic storage. Each layout provides a distinct type for the same logical counter API.

Sixty four bit local operations for the local backed layout named LOCAL64_INIT plus local64_read and local64_set and local64_inc and local64_dec and local64_add and local64_sub plus test forms local64_sub_and_test and local64_dec_and_test and local64_inc_and_test and local64_add_negative plus returning forms local64_add_return and local64_sub_return and local64_inc_return plus conditional forms local64_cmpxchg and local64_try_cmpxchg and local64_xchg and local64_add_unless and local64_inc_not_zero each delegate to the corresponding local counter operation on the wrapped member.

Sixty four bit local operations for the atomic backed layout named LOCAL64_INIT plus local64_read and local64_set and local64_inc and local64_dec and local64_add and local64_sub plus test forms local64_sub_and_test and local64_dec_and_test and local64_inc_and_test and local64_add_negative plus returning forms local64_add_return and local64_sub_return and local64_inc_return plus conditional forms local64_cmpxchg and local64_try_cmpxchg and local64_xchg and local64_add_unless and local64_inc_not_zero each delegate to the matching atomic sixty four bit operation on the wrapped member.

Non atomic sixty four bit helpers for both layouts named __local64_inc and __local64_dec and __local64_add and __local64_sub implement read plus modify plus write through the plain sixty four bit read and set operations without atomicity. Callers must provide exclusion where concurrent updates are possible, while the plain sixty four bit operations delegate to atomic or local primitives that need no extra lock.
The architecture page frame offset named ARCH_PFN_OFFSET has numeric value zero in the generic flat model.

Frame conversions named __pfn_to_page and __page_to_pfn have three alternative models, with shared helpers named __phys_to_pfn and __pfn_to_phys and page_to_pfn and pfn_to_page and phys_to_page. The flat model derives a page pointer from a frame number by offsetting a base map named mem_map with the frame minus the architecture offset, and derives a frame number by the inverse distance plus offset. The virtual map model adds the frame number to a base named vmemmap and subtracts the base for the inverse. The sparse model resolves a section from the page flags or frame number and then offsets within the section map. Shared helpers map between physical addresses and frame numbers, alias page to frame and frame to page to the active model, and map a physical address to a page through the frame number.

Validity helpers named pfn_valid and for_each_valid_pfn clamp frame numbers to the populated range using the architecture offset plus a total mapped count named max_mapnr. The single check reports true only when the frame is at or above the offset and its distance below the total count. The iterator walks from the larger of the requested start and the offset up to the smaller of the requested end and the offset plus total count. A self named marker records that the generic validity check is active.

Page to physical helpers named page_to_phys have checked and unchecked forms. The checked form derives the frame number, emits a one time warning when the frame fails the validity check, and then converts the frame to a physical address. The unchecked form converts directly without validation. Callers that cannot guarantee validity must use the checked form or validate beforehand to avoid translating an invalid page.

A state accessor named __mmiowb_state has two alternative forms, one yielding the raw per CPU pointer via an operation named raw_cpu_ptr to a variable named __mmiowb_state and another delegating to a constructor named arch_mmiowb_state. Both provide the calling CPU ordering state for memory mapped I O write barrier handling.

Inclusion guards named _ASM_GENERIC_IOCTL_H and __GENERIC_IO_H and __ASM_GENERIC_IRQ_H and _ASM_GENERIC_IRQ_REGS_H and _ASM_GENERIC_KDEBUG_H and __ASM_GENERIC_KEXEC_HANDOVER_H and _ASM_GENERIC_KMAP_SIZE_H and _ASM_GENERIC_KPROBES_H and _ASM_GENERIC_KVM_PARA_H and _ASM_GENERIC_LOCAL_H and _ASM_GENERIC_LOCAL64_H and __ASM_MEMORY_MODEL_H and __ASM_GENERIC_MMIOWB_H each record presence of their header and prevent repeated inclusion.

Mapping failure handling requires null checks. The uncached and no populate variants always yield null in the shown generic forms, and port mapping yields null when the masked port exceeds its upper bound. Callers must treat a null device address as failure and must not dereference it. Unmapping companions perform no action and require no pairing behavior beyond accepting the address.
External per CPU read operation owned by another dossier and relied upon for interrupt frame access.
External per CPU write operation owned by another dossier and relied upon for interrupt frame installation.
Probe metadata section names are _kprobe_blacklist for the exclusion list and .kprobes.text for probe text.
